question: GG versus Skia performance rendering Hacker News, including precise native scrolling
conclusion: GG adapters preserve pixels and have essentially identical continuous native publication FPS. Main-process load/capture instructions increase by 2.8044%. Wall-time variation prevents a renderer speedup claim.

scope.selection: One GG-enabled executable with VOX_GG_TEXT/SHAPES/PATHS unset versus all three =1; fallback and unmigrated Skia paths remain.
scope.load: Main browser process, all threads, process creation through the native encoded document PNG checkpoint; startup/window setup, page scripting/layout/paint and PNG encoding included. Filter helpers, GPU work and external services excluded. Not a total-browser coalition measurement or isolated raster cost.
scope.native_first_frame: Navigation and document installation to native layer submission; includes scripting/style/layout and native rendering; not isolated raster cost or physical scanout.
scope.scroll: Changed Cocoa layer publications after updateLayer, over the full first-to-last precise-input period; not physical scanout
scope.workload: Archived Hacker News homepage, original scripts and resources, loopback no-store replay, fresh profiles/caches, retained OS caches, 1024x768 document, native scale 2; same executable and C mode for both variants
scope.schedule: 600 precise native events at nominal 60 Hz, delta 3 (observed 6.5 CSS px/event), reverse every 60 inputs; 4 alternating pairs, 4s title-based settling. Load pairs settle 2s and use screenshot-mode chrome84; normal scroll chrome112. Both audit a 1024x768 document, scale2.
scope.pixel_scope: Load PNGs compare every document RGBA pixel against independently repeated Skia reference; final scroll view PNGs compare outside only the existing 224x24 logical RAM status area. Final PNG encoding occurs after timing/counter endpoints.
scope.cache_network: Complete archived HN homepage and original scripts/resources over the same loopback no-store server per cohort; fresh private caches/profiles each launch; OS caches retained. No pixel references or tolerances relaxed.
scope.javascript: Default JavaScriptCore in both modes; separate post-execution diagnostics report enabled=true runtime=true sources=1 source_bytes=5217 preloaded_scripts=1, and content audits report no JavaScript errors. No LibJS comparison.

limitations: No whole-browser Skia replacement comparison: adapters still fall back and recording/picture paths use Skia.
Instruction results count main browser process only, all threads, consistently in both modes. Filter helpers, GPU and external-service CPU excluded.
Wall times varied substantially under other sessions and compilation on an 18-CPU host; all per-trial loads and order retained. No isolated renderer speedup or broad optimization acceptance claimed.
Continuous throughput around 59.90 FPS coexists with median p95 intervals22.18/20.12ms, maximum32.19/37.42ms and about47.8/46.8% intervals above 16.667 ms (Skia/GG); not a smooth physical60Hz claim.
Hardware-counter scrolling is separate diagnostic-only: one sample per variant per protocol, not a CPU optimization acceptance cohort.
Raw load pixel reference is Skia in the same Vox bundle, not Brave.
Shared bundle may advance after the comparison publication lease releases.
